summary:
This bill is a joint resolution, which is a type of proposal that can become a law if Congress passes it and the president signs it. 

The bill is about a bird called the lesser prairie-chicken. In November 2022, a government group called the United States Fish and Wildlife Service made a rule. This rule put the lesser prairie-chicken on the official list of threatened and endangered animals. When an animal is on this list, it gets special government protections so it does not go extinct, or die out forever. The rule split the birds into two groups. It labeled the northern group as "threatened" and the southern group as "endangered."

This bill says that Congress does not approve of that rule. If this bill becomes a law, it will completely cancel the rule. The rule would have no power or effect. This means the lesser prairie-chicken would not get the specific threatened and endangered protections that were decided in the November 2022 rule.
